newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal agrees to head Brazzaville peace force.
newsitem.headline: Senegal agrees to head Brazzaville peace force.

text.p: Senegal has agreed to command a multinational mainly African peacekeeping force which will eventually deploy in the embattled Congo Republic capital Brazzaville, military sources said on Tuesday.

"The president of the republic has just accepted a request from the United Nations that our country take part in this force and take command of it," one source said, adding that the West African nation would contribute 500 troops.

Political and ethnic fighting and indiscriminate shelling between supporters of President Pascal Lissouba and his predecessor Denis Sassou Nguesso have killed hundreds of people in Brazzaville since the showdown began on June 5.
The U.N. Security Council authorised U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan to sound out mainly African countries about setting up a force of about 1,700 men.
Former colonial power France, whose troops evacuated almost 6,000 foreign nationals from Brazzaville, has offered logistical support for such a force.
Both national and international mediators have been trying to broker a lasting truce in the city and bring the two sides around the negotiating table, so far without success.
Togo has also offered to contribute troops to the force.

Both Senegal and Togo are serving with a similar African peacekeeping force in the capital of the Central African Republic, which borders the Congo Republic and is another former French colony plagued by political and ethnic unrest.
